evidence_class: measured (one 12-job batch run per arm per config; per-job walls tight within runs, see raw.jsonl)

reading.monotone_in_workers: throughput rises with worker count at fixed budget for both arms
reading.threads_vs_workers: at equal W*H, more workers with fewer threads wins (8x1 > 4x2 > 2x4 > 1x8 on candidate): the kernel mix is dominated by per-origin Dijkstra without intra-job numba parallelism at this workload scale
reading.wave_packing_note: 12 jobs / 8 workers leaves the second wave 4/8 packed; 4x2 packs 3 full waves of 4 - and 8x1 still wins, so the choice is not a packing artifact
reading.memory: max worker phase RSS ~350 MB across all configs; 8x1 shows NO memory regression (319 MB)

selected_rationale: highest measured throughput on both arms (cand 3.915, base 2.848 jobs/s), within budget (8*1=8<=8), no memory regression; final alternating-order confirmation follows in T11 before freeze
scope_note: selection is for THIS campaign's admitted workloads regime (W3 accessibility); flow path measured only via stage model + L2 scope, not batch-swept (recorded as a limitation)
